note: Overlapping low-efficiency opening range with no swings/H2-L2 and price pinned near EMA: no qualifying 2nd entry appears; staying flat all window is correct, not passivity.
Lone 50-pt climactic bear spike into session low followed by a weak 3-bar bounce inside a two-sided range — no follow-through case, so no entry either direction. Correct to wait.

Gap-down AIS day but the down move was choppy with heavy bar overlap (efficiency ~0.2-0.55, always-in flipping to neutral bars 10-12) and oversized/climactic bear bars (bars 15-16 both ~14pt outside/trend bars on lows). No clean 2nd-entry short set up with-trend, and bull bars (9, 17) were just bounces in chop. Standing aside all session was the correct read — a bear bias alone doesn't justify chasing extended or climactic bars, and a choppy range with no confirmed pullback structure offers no edge.

Double top was at the session high but the bot entered short on the break of the session low (long-held support) — selling the bottom of a choppy range. In an extreme TR, short the double top near the high targeting the low, or stand aside; do not short the neckline break at the range low.

After a choppy gap-down trading range, a clean 3-bar bull spike reclaiming above EMA is a valid long, but entering late in the spike (bar 14, price already ~6903 after running from 6869) buys near exhaustion into the prior range's overhead supply — the pullback tagged the tight ~8.5pt stop. Consider requiring a first pullback (2nd entry) rather than entering on spike continuation when the move has already traveled 30+ pts off the low.

Gap-up that immediately sells off into an overlapping low-efficiency range (efficiency ~0.20, overlap ~0.64, alternating SH/SL swings) offers no clean KB setup — always-in kept flipping (AIS bars 3-11, neutral/AIL bars 12-19). Correct read is to sit out the whole opening window rather than fade chop; bars 20-23 rightly gated too_late_in_window.

Gap-down reversed into a persistent overlapping bull channel; bot stayed flat all day citing choppy texture and buying-at-highs. In a confirmed always-in-long grind, look harder for a valid 2nd-entry long (H2/L2 pullback to EMA) rather than defaulting to no_trade — zero trades in a 35pt trend is under-participation, not caution.

Bilateral range: gap-down open, swings ping-pong (LL 6957 / HH 6989), efficiency <0.4, always-in neutral. Correctly took zero trades. Doji signal bars (b7,9,16), oversized reversal chase (b8 18.25pt off session low), and a near-magnet short (b12 closing 1.75pt above prior low) were all properly rejected. In extreme two-sided chop with no completed MTR, no signal is a valid outcome.

Strong AIL bull spike-to-channel day, gap +46.5, EMA rising, price held well above EMA bars 1-17. Bot skipped every long and traded nothing. Next time on a clean always-in-long day, treat the first shallow pullback that holds above a rising EMA as a valid 2nd-entry long rather than waiting for a perfect bar — don't let 'too early / chase / near high' objections stack into total inaction.

The bot passed the entire opening bear spike (bars 5-11) because every bar was a with-trend sell into an extended move with no 2nd-entry short pullback and no completed MTR for a countertrend long. Standing aside a fast one-directional spike you didn't get positioned in early is correct — chasing bar 6/7/11 (large bars closing on lows / new session lows) would have been climax-chasing into oversized bars. No pullback short setup ever formed.

After the spike stalled ~6956, bars 12-19 became choppy two-sided rotation around a flattening EMA (bull/bear bars alternating, AI flipping AIS/neutral, closes mid-range). Correctly took nothing: no clean KB setup, magnets (flat EMA, session mid) nearby, and signal bars were dojis/mid-range. Bar-19 cutoff then closed the window. Doing nothing in a structureless range is the disciplined outcome, not a missed trade.

setup: no_trade discipline in a post-spike overlapping range
note: Gap-up spike that immediately rolls over and starts overlapping (overlap ~0.6, no follow-through, always-in flipping bar-to-bar) is a trading range, not a trend. Tempting bull trend bars near the session high (bar12/13/15/19) are chases into the top of the range or into magnets, not 2nd-entry setups. Staying flat and eating no losses is the correct, repeatable outcome here — don't manufacture a fade or a breakout entry just to be in.

Range-fade short at the top of a tight overlapping range was sound in direction, but the stop was set below the true session high (7005) rather than above it, so a retest of the high stopped it out at ~1R. For double-top fades: stop a tick above the higher top, and confirm target keeps R:R comfortably >1 before entering.
